name: Folk Art
summary: Naive hand-painted folk art: warm cream ground, flat red/blue/green/yellow fills, ink brush strokes, decorative floral and geometric borders, and lettering that looks painted by a careful amateur.
whenToUse: When the user asks for folk art, naive or hand-painted charm, decorative floral/geometric borders, warm primary colors with a flat finish, a heartfelt handmade craft or heirloom aesthetic, or a warm painted alternative to flat corporate UI.
rules: Paint flat, never shade: every shape is one opaque pigment fill inside one 3px ink stroke — no gradients, no gloss, no airbrushed highlight, no alpha layers for depth.
Keep the cream ground honest (#f7f0e1 body, #fffcf3 cards) and let only the five pigments — red #c0392b, blue #2c5f8a, green #4f7a4a, yellow #e8b32a, ink #2b2b2b — sit on top of it.

Draw a decorative border around the work: a 3px ink rule echoing the container radius, 4–8px inset from the edge, optionally doubled by a spaced ring of small painted motifs (petal, leaf, berry) that stops at the corners rather than cutting through them.
Round generously — 18px on cards, wells, and media, full pills on buttons and badges — because naive brushwork never produces a sharp machined corner.

Set headings in Fredoka 700 Title Case at 20px and up with slight positive letter-spacing (0.01em), body in Fredoka 400/500 at 16–18px/1.6, and reserve IBM Plex Mono for quantities, dates, and ledger-like data.

Spend one pigment per role: red #c0392b is the primary stroke and action, blue #2c5f8a is the secondary action, link, and focus ring, yellow #e8b32a is highlight and attention, green #4f7a4a is confirmation, #a32e22 is reserved for failure.
Move like a hand, not a machine: 160–280ms easing with a single soft overshoot at most, a gentle 2px lift on hover, and no shimmering, blinking, parallax, or looping animation.

Stay evocation-only: motifs are drawn from primitives (petal = three arcs, leaf = pointed oval, berry = circle, vine = sine path, star = four diamonds) — never copy a specific artwork, plate, canvas, or motif set from any painter or museum collection.
Label with words before color: every pigment-coded state also carries a short human sentence ('Saved', 'Needs a look', 'That went wrong') so the warmth never costs clarity.

componentRecipes.panel: background: #fffcf3; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 18px; padding: 28px; color: #2b2b2b; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #2b2b2b, inset 0 0 0 3px #f7f0e1; position: relative; — the inset cream ring is the painted border; add ::before with inset: 8px; border: 1px dashed #8b7c66; border-radius: 14px; pointer-events: none for a double painted rule, and a heading that sits on a 10px #e8b32a highlight block behind its last word; below 640px drop the 4px 4px 0 ink drop and keep both rules.
componentRecipes.button: font: 700 18px/1 'Fredoka', 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 14px 26px; border-radius: 999px; background: #c0392b; color: #fffcf3; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #2b2b2b; transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), background-color 160ms linear; :hover { transform: translate(-2px, -2px); box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #2b2b2b; } :active { transform: translate(4px, 4px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #2b2b2b; } :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2c5f8a; outline-offset: 3px; } — secondary variant: background #fffcf3, color #2b2b2b, box-shadow 4px 4px 0 #2c5f8a; disabled: background #efe4cd, color #8b7c66, border-color #8b7c66, shadow 0 0 0, no transform, cursor not-allowed.
componentRecipes.input: font: 16px/1.6 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #2b2b2b; background: #f7f0e1; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 18px; padding: 12px 18px; box-shadow: inset 0 3px 0 rgba(43,43,43,.10); :placeholder { color: #8b7c66; font-style: normal; } :focus { background: #fffcf3; outline: 3px solid #2c5f8a; outline-offset: 2px; } — numeric fields use 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace at 16px so ledgers align; invalid: border-color #a32e22 plus a 16px Fredoka sentence below in #a32e22 ('That needs a number here.') and a 6px red painted underline, so the error never depends on hue alone.
componentRecipes.statusbar: height: 52px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; padding: 0 28px; background: #f7f0e1; border-top: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 18px 18px 0 0; font: 15px/1.4 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #2b2b2b; a 3px dashed #8b7c66 rule runs just under the top border as a painted trim; left side lists states each led by a 10px painted dot — #4f7a4a saved, #e8b32a needs attention, #a32e22 failed, #8b7c66 idle — with the state word beside it; right side pairs the mono count ('12 of 40') with the one primary button.
componentRecipes.menu: vertical list, no bullets, 6px gap: item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 18px; font: 600 18px/1.3 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; color: #2b2b2b; background: #fffcf3; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 18px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #2b2b2b; } selected row fills #e8b32a with ink text, gains a 4px #c0392b check mark and a small painted petal motif at its left edge; hover lifts translate(-2px, -2px) to box-shadow 6px 6px 0 #2b2b2b; group headers are Fredoka 700 13px uppercase with letter-spacing 0.14em in #8b7c66 between two 3px dotted rules.
componentRecipes.fieldset: the signature framed block: border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 18px; padding: 24px 28px; background: #fffcf3; legend { font: 700 18px/1 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 0 12px; color: #2b2b2b; background: #fffcf3; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; border-radius: 999px; } with a painted vine drawn behind the legend on the top rule (3px solid #4f7a4a, two 8px #c0392b petal arcs flanking the legend) so the border reads as hand-embellished rather than machine-drawn.
componentRecipes.badge: display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 999px; border: 3px solid #2b2b2b; background: #f7f0e1; color: #2b2b2b; font: 600 14px/1.2 'Fredoka', system-ui, sans-serif; a leading 10px painted dot carries the pigment (#4f7a4a / #e8b32a / #a32e22 / #2c5f8a) and the label always spells the state out — badges never rely on their dot to communicate.

copywriting.voice: A warm, naive, gently earnest maker talking to a neighbour across a kitchen table: plain sentences, second person, present tense, no jargon, and quiet pride in the work. Copy names the object and the feeling ('Your border is painted.', 'This page is not saved yet — shall we keep it?') rather than reporting system state, and it never scolds: a mistake is described kindly and followed by the next small step.

case.commands: sentence case imperative ('Paint the border', 'Keep this page')

avoid: deadpan system errors ('Invalid input.', 'An error occurred.', 'Error 422')
sarcasm, blame, or scolding the user ('You broke it', 'Wrong again')
cutesy diminutives and baby talk ('oopsie', 'whoopsie-doodle', 'aw shucks')
emoji, ASCII art, and decorative dingbats inside headings or buttons
ticket ids, hex hashes, stack traces, and log noise in user-facing copy
all-caps sentences of any length — the voice is quiet, not shouted

do: Frame the content: give every major container a painted border — 3px ink rule plus a 4–8px inset cream ring or dashed echo — so the interface looks bordered and cared for, like a painted plate or a sampler.
Fill flat with one pigment per shape inside one ink stroke, and let flatness be the style; a single soft paper-grain overlay may sit on the ground, but never on top of type.
Keep the cream ground (#f7f0e1, cards #fffcf3) and treat the five pigments as the whole palette; muted text is #8b7c66, not a grey.
Round generously (18px containers, full pills on buttons and badges) and give interactive elements a 4px ink drop that shrinks as the element presses in.
Set headings in Fredoka 700 Title Case from 20px up and body in Fredoka 400/500 at 16–18px/1.6; use IBM Plex Mono only for quantities, dates, and ledger data.

Draw motifs from primitives — petal (three arcs), leaf (pointed oval), berry (circle), vine (sine path), star (four diamonds) — and place them at borders, corners, and empty states, never as decoration in the middle of a sentence.
Speak kindly and plainly: describe what happened and the next small step ('This page is not saved yet — shall we keep it?').
Animate like a hand: one gentle 160–280ms transition and at most a 2px hover lift; every state change must remain legible with motion turned off.
dont: No reproduced artworks: no painting, sampler, plate, pattern, or motif set copied from any folk artist, museum, or archive — evocation through palette, border, and naive geometry only.
No gradients, glassmorphism, backdrop-blur, semi-transparent overlays, or airbrushed shading; a shape is one flat fill inside one ink stroke.
No blurred shadow stacks, glow, or neon; the only permitted softness is the single 0 6px 14px rgba(43,43,43,.10) floating-panel lift and the soft edge vignette.
No sharp 0-radius cards, no hairline 1px rules, no machined grid lines — the smallest line weight in the system is 3px ink, and corners are round.
No pixelation, scanlines, CRT effects, or dithering; this aesthetic is painted, not rendered.
No second pigment inside one component as pure decoration; one role color plus ink, and never more than three pigments in a single card.
No fast, bouncy, springy, looping, blinking, or parallax motion — nothing that reads as a toy or a game cabinet.
No snark, no shouting, no cutesy baby talk, and no emoji standing in for a label.
accessibility: Ink #2b2b2b on cream #f7f0e1 clears 4.5:1 easily, and white #fffcf3 on red #c0392b is about 5:1, but yellow #e8b32a, green #4f7a4a, and blue #2c5f8a mostly do not carry cream text — use those as fills, borders, dots, and large bold labels, and set any text inside them in ink #2b2b2b.

Fredoka and Baloo 2 stay at 16px minimum for body and 20px for headings with 1.5–1.6 line-height; Chewy is a display fallback only and must never carry a paragraph, a form value, or a navigation label.

Honor prefers-reduced-motion: remove the hover lift, the press translate, and every transition duration, keeping only instant state changes, and replace any soft vignette drift with a static background.

Never signal state with pigment alone — pair each dot, badge, and border with a written state ('Saved', 'Needs attention', 'Failed', 'Idle'), and keep a visible 3px #2c5f8a focus ring at 3px offset on every focusable element.
Decorative borders, vines, and motif glyphs are aria-hidden and carry no meaning; if a motif is the only content of a control, give that control an accessible name.
signatureElement: The hand-painted decorative border: a 3px ink rule with an inset cream ring, an optional dashed echo, and small painted petal/leaf/berry motifs stopping at the rounded corners — the frame that makes every panel read as a made object rather than a div

prose.overview: Folk Art paints the interface as something made by hand and meant to be kept: a warm cream ground, flat reds and blues and greens, ink brush strokes, and a decorative border around every panel. The charm is naive on purpose — corners are round, spacing breathes, motifs are simple petals and leaves — while the grid underneath stays disciplined so the page still reads cleanly. It should feel heartfelt, domestic, and unhurried, like a painted plate or a stitched sampler hung where everyone can see it, never like a folk-pattern skin stamped onto a dashboard.
prose.colors: The ground is warm cream #f7f0e1 with cards a shade brighter at #fffcf3, and ink #2b2b2b draws every stroke and carries nearly all text, with #8b7c66 as the only muted tone. Five pigments do the talking: red #c0392b for the primary action and the painted frame, blue #2c5f8a for the secondary action, links, and focus, green #4f7a4a for leaves and confirmation, yellow #e8b32a for highlights and attention, and the deeper #a32e22 held back for failure. Nothing is blended — a shape is one flat fill inside one ink stroke, exactly like paint laid down once — and the pigment ramps give each hue a light/base/dark triad for pressed and wash states rather than a gradient.
prose.typography: Fredoka leads with its soft, slightly irregular terminals, backed by Baloo 2 and Chewy as the friendly fallbacks, at 700 weight in Title Case from 20px up with a touch of positive letter-spacing so headings feel painted rather than tightened. Body copy drops to Fredoka 400/500 at 16–18px with 1.6 line-height — generous, because a hand-lettered page is never dense. IBM Plex Mono appears only where numbers must line up, such as quantities, dates, and ledger rows, and never for prose; italics and faux weights are avoided because a brush has one voice.
prose.layout: Layout rides a calm scale of 4/8/16/28/44px on a 12-column grid with 28px gutters, and every major region sits inside its own painted container instead of bleeding into the next. Content is centred with real margins and a visible outer frame, so the page reads like a bordered panel or a framed print rather than a full-bleed canvas; borders are inset 4–8px from the container edge and echo its 18px radius at the corners. Sequences stack vertically with a small motif instead of a numbered rail, and nothing is optically nudged: the warmth lives in the border and the motif, never in a misaligned box.
prose.elevation: Depth is minimal and physical: a 4px 4px 0 #2b2b2b ink drop under cards, buttons, and rows, which collapses to 0 0 0 as the element translates into it on press, plus one low soft lift (0 6px 14px rgba(43,43,43,.10)) allowed only for a floating dialog or drag ghost. Inside containers the only depth is a single inset rule, inset 0 3px 0 rgba(43,43,43,.10), for wells like inputs, and a soft radial vignette darkening the outer edge of the page by a few percent. There are no gloss highlights, no layered blurred shadows, no glass, and no glow — light is a wash, not a light source.
prose.shapes: Shapes are round and generous: 18px radius on cards, wells, media, and fieldsets, full pills on buttons, badges, and legends, and a consistent 3px #2b2b2b stroke around every shape so each element looks drawn around rather than filled to an edge. Motifs come from primitives — three arcs for a petal, a pointed oval for a leaf, a circle for a berry, a sine path for a vine, four diamonds for a star — and appear at borders, corners, dividers, and empty states with decorative meaning, not as confetti in the middle of text. Sharp 0-radius cards, 1px hairlines, and machined square corners have no place here; the smallest line weight in the system is 3px ink.
prose.components: Panels are cream cards with a 3px ink stroke, an inset cream ring, an optional dashed echo 8px inside, and a 4px hard drop, with the heading sitting on a yellow highlight block. Buttons are ink-stroked pills in red whose drop shrinks under the press, with a cream secondary that keeps a blue drop so it still reads as a made object. Inputs are sunken cream wells with an ink stroke that brighten to #fffcf3 and take a blue outline on focus, fieldsets wear a painted vine behind their pill legend, and the status bar is a friendly ledger — dot plus a written state word on the left, a mono count and the single primary button on the right.
prose.dosDonts: Do frame every container with a painted border, do fill flat with one pigment per shape inside one ink stroke, do keep the cream ground and the five-pigment palette, and do let the voice stay warm, plain, and forgiving. Don't reproduce any actual artwork, sampler, or motif set, don't reach for gradients, glass, glow, scanlines, or pixelation, don't sharpen a corner or drop to a 1px hairline, and don't copy the charm with cutesy baby talk or shout it in all caps.
